title: Integrated Development of Spatial Regeneration and the Cultural and Creative Industries in Chinese Traditional Villages: A Correlational Literature Review
content: Spatial regeneration and the cultural and creative industries (CCIs) are paired in policies for China’s traditional villages, yet seldom examined together. This correlational literature review analyzes the full texts of 35 peer-reviewed case studies published in 2017–2026. The corpus was assembled purposively; a later check of two bibliographic databases flagged at least 238 further potentially eligible records, so the 35 papers cover only part of the literature. Each paper was coded for regeneration strategies, CCI categories, village type, governance mode, outcomes, and conflicts, and the analysis combines keyword co-occurrence, φ coefficients, and a qualitative classification of outcomes. Five of six regeneration strategies are reported in more than two-thirds of the papers. Cultural tourism is reported in every paper, followed by performing arts, crafts, and museums, whereas architecture, design, film, and digital content appear in eight papers. No strategy–category association remains significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Of 140 outcome judgments, 47.1% are realized positive, 35.7% mixed, and 10.0% realized negative; negative results concentrate in the social dimension. The sample is too small to test differences by region, village type, or governance mode. In these papers, the link between spatial regeneration and cultural activity is documented almost exclusively through tourism.
